recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed unless a future core build is shown not to consume the corrected THO terminology package; any remaining source maintenance for this exact definition belongs in THO/UTG.
issue_request: FHIR-34389 was an Applied FHIR-core Security change request with a Persuasive with Modification resolution asking to change the Provenance agent type code enterer from "A person entering the data into the originating system" to "An agent entering the data into the originating system, such as a scribe or transcriptionist."
initial_application: The old core CodeSystem source once contained the stale person-specific enterer definition, but commit 5c0494aacfd0b8bd52bc72c587aa89d0a64246f8 removed UTG-maintained terminology content, including source/provenance/codesystem-provenance-agent-type.xml, from the core build. Current core source keeps Provenance in build scope and binds through a value set that includes the external THO provenance-agent-type value set.
additional_context: UP-524, a THO/UTG Proposal Implemented issue, explicitly grouped FHIR-34389 with related Provenance agent type cleanup, was approved by the Security WG on 2024-02-19, and modified input/sourceOfTruth/fhir/codeSystems/CodeSystem-provenance-participant-type.xml. Current THO JSON for CodeSystem/provenance-participant-type, including the 6.0.2-era path checked separately, contains the requested enterer definition.
reconciliation: No FHIR core source change was made. The authoritative concept definition belongs to THO/UTG, and the external source of truth already says: "An agent entering the data into the originating system, such as a scribe or transcriptionist."
